text: On the early printed carrier one underside member failed to print and another snapped under finger pressure. The side was uncertain.
Use a smooth rounded index-finger contact surface that shields the exposed key contacts and lets the finger rest close to the rod.
Support the finger across the middle of the guard, connecting the middle to the edges as well as the corners. Keep both sides similarly supported where possible.
Protect fingers from the metal underneath the keys with comfortable, rounded, integral wireframe beams. Both outside edges need support from below. The guard must withstand normal finger pressure.

Give the lower finger guards a gentle, genuinely rounded slope into the body, blending sooner so no lower edge juts out. Check the skin-contact surface below the lower keys for a lip, poking corner or sharp V-shaped edge.
Minimise material extending past the lower row where the index finger rests while protecting it from the key undersides.

A small increase in guard-to-base clearance may make finger and socket assembly easier while preserving the accepted smooth rounded integral beams. The user withdrew moving the guards inward and later assembled the socket successfully; do not treat the withdrawn direction as adopted geometry.

Keep the complete exposed bottom edge of the key holder and finger-contact guard smoothly rounded all the way around, as generously as space and strength permit. Preserve the earlier blend into the body; inspect the full perimeter in the finished model and assembly diagram, not only one section.

Give both lower key banks matching smooth, rounded fork branches in three dimensions. Use the other side as the shape reference, including the underside and the bend into the body. Keep pointed ends, cut-off tips and protrusions off the finger surface. Preserve two separated roots, contact shielding and space to fit the prewired black socket. At the click end opposite the battery entrance, match the long rounded branch where the index finger rests. Compare the two curves from the same underside angle. Copy the contact curve nearest the rod directly. Only change a branch locally where a fitted part or its required installation path demonstrably interferes. The battery does not have to exit through the finger rest.
